fulminant.et: From Latin fulmināns (“striking with lightning”) via French fulminant.

Fülle.et: From Middle High German vülle, from Old High German fullī. Equivalent to voll + -e.

füllen.et: From Middle High German vüllen, from Old High German fullen. Compare Dutch vullen, English fill, Danish fylde, Swedish fylla.

Füllen.et: From Middle High German vülīn, fülīn, from Old High German fulīn, from Proto-Germanic *fulīną, diminutive of Proto-Germanic *fulô (whence modern German Fohlen). The two forms were later perceived as mere phonetic variants; see Fohlen for more.

Fulda.et: From Old High German Vulthaha, Vuldaha, from Proto-Germanic *fuldō (“earth, field, plain”) + *ahwō (“water”).
